name: Free Reading Data Fifth Grade Lesson PowerPoint Template
description: A free, editable fifth-grade data literacy lesson with a question, sample survey, chart reading, comparison, practice, and exit ticket.
longDescription: This original eight-slide lesson helps a teacher introduce fifth-grade students to reading and discussing simple survey data. The story moves from a question and learning goal through an illustrative class survey, a bar comparison, a guided reading method, partner practice, a check for misleading scales, and an exit ticket. A warm paper background, deep plum type, mint data tiles, and a clear ledger grid are built entirely from native editable PowerPoint shapes. All counts are explicitly illustrative; replace them with actual classroom data before teaching.
cover: A classroom lesson in reading, comparing, and questioning sample survey results.

story.title: Begin with one answerable question
story.body: Which reading spot does our sample group prefer? First agree on what each response means.

story.title: A small survey becomes a data set
story.body: Use these invented responses to practice before collecting real classroom answers.

story.title: Look for the largest and smallest groups
story.body: Read the labels and scale before making a claim about the sample results.

story.title: Read a chart in three careful passes
story.body: A repeatable routine makes the evidence easier to explain and check.
points: Use a number to support it

story.title: Ask a partner to test your claim
story.body: Write one comparison, swap explanations, and check the arithmetic together.

story.title: A short axis can exaggerate a gap
story.body: Compare the same sample counts on a scale that starts at zero before interpreting size.

story.title: Explain one finding and one limit
story.body: Use a sample number to support your answer, then name what the class still needs to learn.
